answer: Sybil resistance rests on bonded collateral escrows: when k identities commit correlated equivocation, the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than as a fixed cost per identity. Detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss through asymmetric depreciation, making a coordinated swarm more costly than isolated misconduct. Splitting stake among identities named mesa, onyx, or opal does not dilute correlated evidence or reduce the aggregate liability.
